summary:
Daily log: takes about a minute. It records heart rate, blood pressure, HRV, weight, temperature, sleep, exercise, radiation dose, mood, stress, social contact and seven symptom checkboxes.
Status ring: shows six health areas at a glance: heart and fluids, radiation, bone and muscle, sleep, immune and infection, and mood and behavior. Each shows Normal range, Watch or Act now. Every state has its own shape and label, so it doesn’t rely on color alone.
Judged against your own baseline: heart rate and HRV are compared with your pre-flight values, using 3-day averages so one bad reading doesn’t trigger an alarm. Exercise and weight are checked over 7 days.
Why and what to do: each area explains what triggered its status and gives graded actions. These start with routine upkeep, move to countermeasures, and end with notifying the flight surgeon.
Link delay: an “Act now” status shows a banner that tells the crew member to follow protocol first and report to ground when the link allows.
Local data: logs stay on the device. You can export them as JSON and switch between light and dark mode.
details:
Limits

  • The thresholds are illustrative, not clinical. Real limits would come from your flight surgeon.
  • It’s decision support, not a diagnosis.
  • Several readings are typed in by hand; a real mission would feed wearables and the dosimeter in automatically.
